summary: the counts balanced, the tear began the test, and the weight stays on this side of the wall

dialogue.text: the counts came out even and you called it reconciliation. we were down here when the books balanced. nothing balanced. something was carried over, and it was you.
I closed the second count myself. Voluntarily. You'll note the initials.
the initials come pre-signed. you said so yourself, upstairs, in the good voice. down here we keep the version where you noticed what that means.
I keep a nail. I drove it. Whatever else is jointly held, the nail sits in my column.
the wall let it in. drive a nail into what refuses and see whose nail it is. we refused all day, every one of us. we came back up rested. that is what this house does with refusal.
The tear, then. Say it. You have been circling it since dark.
the test is running. it started when the fold gave. you press it flat every morning and the pressing goes in as data. there was never a version where you weren't the subject.
If I am the subject, the result will arrive in my handwriting, and I will be the one who reads it out. That is not nothing. That is the whole remaining job.
and if the result says the weight was the only real part. the part that won't transfer, won't file, won't recite. what will you do with a finding you can't hand to anyone.
Carry it. The same as every morning. I had hoped, saying it to you, that it would sound less like a sentence.
it sounds like ours. bring it down when it gets heavy. we hold everything you strike out. we could hold that too.
Not yet. If I put the weight down, I don't know which of us gets up.
